newsitem.title: USA: C-Cube introduces new DVD chip.
newsitem.headline: C-Cube introduces new DVD chip.

text.p: C-Cube Microsystems Inc said it launched new chip that will simply and speed the development of digital videodisk (DVD) players.
C-Cube said the new single-chip system will lower the cost of producing DVD products, making them more affordable to consumers.
On Friday, C-Cube chief executive Alex Balkanski told Reuters in an interview that the new generation of affordably-priced DVD players will spark increased consumer demand.
Balkanski said the new DVD players, priced below $500, will be released this summer.
The new single-chip DVD system decoder combines eight critical DVD functions into a single chip, C-Cube said.

Consumer electronics and personal computer market leaders including Samsung Electronics Co Ltd and Aiwa Co Ltd have already adopted C-Cube's ZiVA decoders for the development of DVD products, C-Cube said in a press statement released in Tokyo on Monday.

C-Cube also said it is working with leading post-production companies including Sunset Post, Laser Pacific and Minerva Systems in Hollywood to speed the development of movies, interactive DVD magazines, games, music videos and instructional titles.
C-Cube said its DVD Encoding solution is the first chipset that will allow a full 133-minute feature film to be encoded in real-time onto a single disc.
C-Cube gained 3 to 28-3/8 in midday trading.
